sŭb-ŏlĕo (-ŏlo ,
I.pres. subj. subolat, Ter. Heaut. 5, 1, 26; cf. oleo init.), ēre, v. n. (prop. to emit a smell; only trop. and in third pers. sing.): hoc subolet alicui, or impers. subolet (alicui), to smell, scent, perceive any thing; I (thou, etc.), perceive, detect, etc. (ante-class.): “id jam pridem sensi et subolet mihi,” Plaut. Ps. 1, 5, 7 ; id. Cas. 2, 3, 59; 3, 2, 24; Ter. Phorm. 3, 1, 10: “propemodum quod illic festinet, sentio et subolet mihi,” Plaut. Trin. 3, 1, 14 Brix ad loc.: “scio equidem te, animatus ut sis: video, subolet, sentio,” id. ib. 3, 2, 72 ; id. Cas. 2, 3, 48.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
